newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower, LSFO pressured.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower, LSFO pressured.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to down slightly Monday in sluggish trade, with low sulphur grades generally undermined by still-ample inventories despite some below-normal East Coast weather.

"The (low sulphur) market is under more pressure. There's not a lot of storage and there's a lot of low sulphur out there," said one cash trader, adding the sharp slide in crude today did not help the bulls.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to the $18.75 a barrel area, with February paper sold early at $18.55 and later at $18.35, off 50 cents with crude.
NYH January one percent paper was offered at $18.50, down more than a quarter from Friday's levels, traders said.
Despite the cold lingering in the East this week, most expected lower prices ahead.
"If anyone tries to bid the market up, there are plenty of guys willing to sell," said another cash trader, adding the whole complex seemed soft.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour slipped more than a quarter to about $20.50 amid steady offers despite prospects for improved utility demand from the weather.
High sulphurs in New York again were unchanged.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent eased slightly to $17.75-18.00, but some thought the number was much lower. USG three percent held steady at $15.75-16.00, traders said.
New York city gate gas prices were talked steady to higher Monday in the $4.50-5.00/mmBtu area on colder East Coast temperatures. NYH one percent resid slipped to a $2.98/mmBtu equivalent.
